messages:
Ashley R: seeing p95 east-west jump to ~320ms across GPU nodes in rack-r7 during the 11:03-11:07 peak batching window. Affects model-serving lanes 4/5.
Maya (oncall): confirming. Grafana shows RDMA retransmits up 6x and if_in_errors on toR-3. Throughput drops but CPU okay.
infra-bot: alert: network.latency.eastwest p95 > 300ms for 4m (hosts: gpu-57,gpu-58,gpu-60).
Sergey: any config changes in that rack? TOR or MTU rollouts?
Maya (oncall): we rolled kernel 5.15.98 on r7 nodes last night and applied a TOR config push (mtu 9000 -> 1500 fallback rule) at 02:10. Could be related.
Ashley R: captured a short packet dump on gpu-58 during spike: `IP length 1500 frag` repeated. Suspect jumbo mismatch / fragmentation.
ops-sre: quick mitigation — pin affected model routes to dedicated capacity or reduce batch window to 16 tokens. That drops efficiency but gets p95 < 80ms. Doable for 30m?
Maya (oncall): will reroute traffic off rack-r7 to rack-r3 for canary, starting in 3m.
Sergey: I'll check RDMA counters and the TOR neighbor MTU. Quick checks: `ethtool -k eth0` and `ip link show` on gpu-58. If we see mtu mismatch, we should revert TOR fallback to 9000 on that leaf.
Ashley R: pasted counters from gpu-58: `RX errors: 124  TX errors: 0  RDMA retransmits: 310` — that feels like local NIC/driver/firmware problem.
Sergey: rolling `ib_core`/`mlx5_core` reload on gpu-58 now. If that doesn't clear, we plan a NIC hotreset via ipmi.
Maya (oncall): reroute done. Initial p95 for the service down to 72ms, but ~10% of jobs retried at source (we're tolerating for now).
ops-sre: good. ETA on NIC reset?
Sergey: NIC reload completed, counters dropping. Waiting 2 minutes to confirm.
infra-bot: update: network.latency.eastwest p95 dropped to 65ms at 2187654352.
Ashley R: nice — keep an eye on RDMA qps for next batch ramp. If it recurs after kernel upgrade we should pin kernel or schedule controlled rollback for r7.
Maya (oncall): noted. Filing follow-up ticket to audit TOR MTU pushes vs kernel changes. Also add a Canary for future kernel rollouts that verifies RDMA counters under synthetic batch load.
Sergey: thumbs up. I'll also open a support case with NIC vendor — fw mismatch/behavior under fragmentation looks suspicious.
Ashley R: thanks everyone. I'll leave the temporary routing in place until the vendor confirms or we decide on rollback :thumbsup:
ops-sre: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will update postmortem with timelines and mitigations.
